_about: Krish's verdicts on titles, and what each teaches. Every title a reader sees first (article, YouTube, Shorts, cover, video title card, card headings) is written against these, offered to Krish as a few options, and used only once he has picked it: scripts/post-pack/title_check.py refuses an asset whose title has no 'picked' verdict here. Record a verdict with `title_check.py verdict`. Krish, 2026-10-14: 'figure out why I dislike it, and iterate, and understand what I actually like, and then encode that into the system forever.'

lessons.lesson: First person beats explaining: put Krish in it (I tried, I tested, I scored).
lessons.from: A2 picked over B, C and D; 'It should be personal ... It could be first person'

lessons.lesson: A question in the middle makes the reader answer before the reveal ('Its rival?').
lessons.from: A2 picked over A1, A3, A4

lessons.lesson: The payoff points at the reader ('your pocket'), not at the companies.
lessons.from: 'I like both elements' (the first person and the pocket line)

lessons.lesson: Short, with the surprise last. Giving the answer early (a score, a tie) kills it.
lessons.from: A2 picked over A3 ('It's a draw') and A4 ('Siri tied it')

lessons.lesson: A reveal that flips what people assume works; a straw man that denies what nobody said does not.
lessons.from: 'Muse's real rival: Siri.' liked; 'Muse vs ChatGPT isn't a fair fight' called dumb

lessons.lesson: Never a textbook label or taxonomy ('Three kinds of AI. Only one runs your errands.'): no person, no tension, no stake.
lessons.from: 'such a boring title ... It should be personal and much more ... more entertaining'

lessons.lesson: A concrete, newsy twist about a named company ('Amazon's already blocked it') beats a privacy 'catch' or a quiz question.
lessons.from: T1 picked over T2 (the catch), T3 (guess which), T4 (A2 reused)

lessons.lesson: Name the subject (Muse) in the title, then a more cryptic promise of what he reveals ('I break down ...'): the name is what people search and recognise; the promise is the open loop.
lessons.from: Krish on the YouTube round: 'we need to name Muse in the title, and then say something more cryptic like "I break down XYZ"'

verdicts.title: I tried Meta's new AI. Amazon's already blocked it.
verdicts.why: first person, then a concrete twist about a named company, surprise last

verdicts.title: I tried Meta's new AI. The catch? Meta can get to your data.
verdicts.why: not picked: the privacy catch is less surprising than Amazon blocking it

verdicts.title: I scored Meta's new AI against Siri. Guess which one knows you better?
verdicts.why: not picked: a quiz question, weaker than a concrete twist

verdicts.title: Muse's real rival: Siri.
verdicts.why: a reveal that flips the assumed fight; short; two names you know
verdicts.krish: I like "Muses' real rival, Siri." on that card

verdicts.title: I tried Meta's new AI. Its rival? Already in your pocket.
verdicts.why: first person; a question mid-title; the payoff points at the reader; surprise last

verdicts.title: I tested Meta's new AI. Its real rival is already in your pocket.
verdicts.why: the right idea, too long and flat: needed punchier

verdicts.title: I put Meta's new AI up against Siri. It's a draw.
I tested Meta's Muse. Siri tied it.
Everyone's comparing Muse to ChatGPT. Wrong fight.
verdicts.why: about other people, not Krish or the reader

verdicts.title: One of these AIs will do your shopping. It isn't ChatGPT.
ChatGPT answers. Cowork works. Muse runs your errands.
verdicts.why: a neat list, no person and no surprise

verdicts.title: Three kinds of AI. Only one runs your errands.
verdicts.why: a textbook taxonomy: boring, impersonal, not entertaining
verdicts.krish: such a boring title. It should be personal and much more. It could be first person. It could be more entertaining. That title is terrible.

verdicts.title: Muse vs ChatGPT isn't a fair fight
verdicts.why: a straw man: denies a claim nobody made
verdicts.krish: no one has ever said "Muse versus ChatGPT" is a fair fight!

verdicts.title: Muse isn't ChatGPT. There are now three kinds of AI.
verdicts.why: states the obvious, as a denial
verdicts.krish: Of course, Muse isn't ChatGPT. That's a stupid thing to say. It's dumb.
